chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Should I supplicate for my parents if they do not recognize the truth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Supplicate for them and give charity on their behalf; and if they are alive and do not recognize the truth, then circle around them (be patient and gentle with them), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah sent me with mercy, not with ingratitude (or disobedience).'

key_terms.الْحَقَّ: The Truth (often referring to Wilayah or Imamate in Shia context)
key_terms.فَدَارِهِمَا: Then circle around them / be patient and gentle with them

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim treat parents who do not accept their faith or Wilayah?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that filial piety extends beyond mere obedience, instructing believers to supplicate and give charity for parents who may not recognize the truth of Wilayah, even if they are alive. He emphasizes a strategy of gentle patience ('circling around them') rather than harsh confrontation, grounding this approach in the Prophetic tradition that Allah sent the Prophet with mercy, not with 'uqq (disobedience/ingratitude). This highlights the Shia principle of maintaining familial bonds with kindness while preserving theological integrity.
